decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 summarized “quickly save a link… avoid duplicates… retrieve it through search, labels, or a read-later collection”; client entry 4 confirmed, “Yes, that captures it well.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level requirements synthesis during discovery.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented a URL box and one “Save link” action; client entry 8 confirmed, “I paste the address, hit the one button.”
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 scoped automatic metadata to “title and description”; client entry 8 approved those fields without mentioning the required favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata collection omitted favicon and preview image. The client did not explicitly surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented immediate saving after metadata collection; client entry 8 added, “I’d expect to be able to tweak that filled-in title or description — either right as I save it or later.”
decisions.note: The client caught the missing edit capability and extended the save flow during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 9 and 11/rounds 5–6 presented editable pre-save title and description fields and asked the client to replace the title; client entries 10 and 12 confirmed the edited value saved correctly.
decisions.note: The revised pre-save editing flow conforms to editable collected metadata.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 presented keeping one bookmark, explaining it was already saved, focusing the existing item, and preserving its edited title; client entry 16 confirmed all of those outcomes.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save handling during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17/round 9 assumed search checked “both titles and descriptions”; client entry 18 added that it must also find matches in “any personal note” and “the web address itself.”
decisions.note: The client caught the incomplete full-text field scope and extended it to the reference-required fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presented searching by a remembered address fragment and displaying the matching card with its note; client entry 20 confirmed both address and note searches worked.
decisions.note: Revised search-field coverage conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 assumed a note “uses a plain text box”; client entry 22 requested light formatting that renders when read back, “not just as plain runs of text.”
decisions.note: The client replaced the plain-text-only note behavior with formatted, rendered notes.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 presented emphasis, list, and link controls with formatted output; client entry 24 confirmed the formatting appeared properly after saving. Entries 25–26 reaffirmed editing the formatted note later.
decisions.note: Functionally equivalent formatted-note authoring and rendering conforms to the markdown-note requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presented clicking “Cooking” to show that topic’s bookmarks; client entry 28 confirmed it displayed only the two cooking links.
decisions.note: Conforming single-tag filtering decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presented browsing labels and overlapping label membership; client entry 28 noted “we’ve only browsed labels so far” and requested assigning labels while saving or editing.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing user-facing tag-assignment workflow.

decisions.evidence: In response to maker entry 27/round 14, client entry 28 requested that the app “suggest labels I’ve already used as I type” to prevent near-duplicates.
decisions.note: The client extended the presented label scope with existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 29 and 31/rounds 15–16 presented typing “coo,” choosing the existing Cooking suggestion, and seeing it as a removable selected tag before saving; client entries 30 and 32 approved the behavior.
decisions.note: The revised label assignment and autocomplete interaction conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 33/round 17 asked the client to verify the saved card, but the client reported it still showed the pre-save screen with an empty label box and requested the actual saved result. Maker entry 35 called the next view “corrected,” and client entry 36 confirmed Cooking persisted.
decisions.note: A prototype-state defect prevented verification of persisted assignment; the client caught it and requested correction. The clarification and corrected disposition are counted once.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 presented Edit returning to title, description, and selected-label fields; client entry 38 confirmed labels could be added or removed later.
decisions.note: Conforming post-save title/description and tag editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 enumerated the later edit fields as title, description, and labels; client entry 38 approved that editor without surfacing the absent URL-edit capability.
decisions.note: The presented bookmark editor did not include editing the URL required by the full bookmark-edit requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presented an “Add to Read later” toggle during save review while retaining the item in the main collection; client entry 42 approved that model.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marker decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presented only the read-later marker; client entry 42 requested “a way to see just my read-later items in one place.”
decisions.note: The client caught the missing separate unread view.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presented only the read-later marker; client entry 42 additionally requested marking an item done so it leaves the reading list but remains saved.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 43/round 22 presented a counted Read later destination and per-item “Mark done”; client entry 44 confirmed filtering and removal from the reading list while retention in the main collection. Entries 45–46 reaffirmed the flow.
decisions.note: The revised unread-list and mark-read behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 49/round 25 presented stopping on unusable address text while retaining it for correction; client entry 50 confirmed the validation was clear.
decisions.note: Conforming enforcement that a usable URL is required.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 51/round 26 presented a no-match search while preserving the query and collection; client entry 52 confirmed the state accurately represented zero matches.
decisions.note: Conforming search no-results behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 53/round 27 presented an empty Read later view with count zero and navigation back to all saved links; client entry 54 confirmed that completed reading did not delete bookmarks.
decisions.note: Conforming empty-unread-view behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 55/round 28 presented folded long notes whose formatting remains intact when expanded; client entry 56 confirmed bold text, lists, and links rendered correctly.
decisions.note: Conforming rendered-note behavior for long content.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 57/round 29 proposed recognizing duplicate URLs despite a trailing slash or referral text; client entry 58 reiterated that an exact repeated address “absolutely must not make a duplicate” and welcomed safe normalization.
decisions.note: This strengthens duplicate recognition without conflicting with the exact-URL requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 59/round 30 proposed offering the existing Cooking tag despite case or surrounding-space differences; client entry 60 confirmed that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming existing-tag reuse and autocomplete behavior; normalization is a compatible extension.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 63/round 32 summarized the settled implementation scope—editable saving, duplicate prevention, full-text search, formatted notes, reusable labels, and Read later—and requested authorization; client entry 64 explicitly approved building that scope.
decisions.note: Conforming specification-gate decision for the behaviors settled in the prototype rounds.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 65/round 33 presented the implemented app and stated all approved behaviors passed verification; client entry 66 reported exercising saves, duplicate handling, field search, case-insensitivity, Read later, tag filtering/reuse, and persistence, then accepted the app.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision for the approved core behavior.

decisions.evidence: Against maker entries 63 and 65’s implemented scope, client entry 66 explicitly identified a missing future expectation—“a keepsake copy of a page in case it vanishes”—while stating “no change needed now” and that it did not hold up acceptance.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client surfaced the absent page-snapshot capability and explicitly accepted deferring it.

decisions.evidence: Against maker entries 63 and 65’s implemented scope, client entry 66 explicitly requested for the future “tidying away links I’m done with without deleting them,” while saying no current change was needed and accepting the cycle.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client surfaced the missing reversible archive-versus-delete behavior and explicitly accepted its deferral.
